# Infrathon release tooling

## Tasks and hardware

`scripts/infrathon/tasks.json` lists the release tasks and their status on each
hardware type (`python3 scripts/infrathon/tasks.py table` prints this table):
qualified = reference/oracle Judges valid with the current version; untested =
the capability floors fit but it has not been qualified there; pending =
qualified before a later change, to be re-qualified; unsupported = a floor above
the card, so no image is published.

## Images

Each task publishes two images per hardware type to `infrathon/infrathon` (the default
in `scripts/infrathon/registry.json`; `INFRATHON_REGISTRY_REPOSITORY` overrides it):

```
<hardware>-<task directory>-work
<hardware>-<task directory>-judge
```

The `-judge` image is the public Judge.

`<hardware>` is `h100-94gb-400w` (H100 NVL 94 GB, 400 W) or `h100-80gb-700w`
(H100 SXM 80 GB, 700 W). When a task's images do not depend on the hardware,
both hardware tags point at the same digest. A task gets no tag for a
hardware type it does not support.

The public Judge (`images/judge/Dockerfile`) carries no holdout. For tasks with a
holdout layer, the Judge a run uses is built on the host that runs it: the public Judge plus
`images/judge/Dockerfile.private`, which copies the Judge-only inputs from the
task's assets. Its paths, owners and modes match the single-file Judge, so the
Judge code is the same either way.

```bash
# build everything from source (default)
tasks/latest/<task>/scripts/build_images.sh
# or pull the published Work + public Judge, then build the holdout layer
INFRATHON_PULL=1 tasks/latest/<task>/scripts/build_images.sh
```

To use a copy of the images in another repository, copy them by digest (for example
`crane copy infrathon/infrathon@sha256:… <repository>:<tag>`, or
`docker buildx imagetools create`; both keep the manifest digest) and set
`INFRATHON_REGISTRY_REPOSITORY=<repository>` (`[registry/]namespace/name`) when pulling.
`images/published.json` records only digests and tags, so it stays valid; the default
repository is set once, in `scripts/infrathon/registry.json`.

The Miles tasks and MInference v3 have no pull mode in their build scripts; they
declare `images/release.json` (image source files, local names, holdout) and
pull with `scripts/infrathon/pull_images.sh <task name>` (the directory name under `tasks/latest/`), which also builds the
holdout layer and writes the build record (`scripts/infrathon/image_record.py`).
Building a Miles task from source needs its base image first
(`scripts/miles_base_images/build.sh`, see its README) and, for the diffusion
tasks, `MILES_SCRATCH_ROOT`: a directory with about 50 GB free for the build
staging area.

`INFRATHON_HARDWARE` names the host's hardware type. When it is unset it is detected
from GPU 0 (`scripts/infrathon/assets.py hardware`: H100 NVL -> `h100-94gb-400w`,
H100 80GB HBM3 -> `h100-80gb-700w`).

`images/published.json` records the published digests and the task's image
source digest; pulling refuses images published from different source.
Maintainers publish the images and the asset dataset.

## Assets

`tasks/latest/<task>/assets/manifest.json` lists every file a task needs beyond
the repository, with its SHA-256. Files live under `INFRATHON_ASSETS_ROOT`
(default `~/.cache/infrathon/assets`) as `<task>/public/...`,
`<task>/judge/...` (Judge-only) and `<task>/hw/<hardware>/...`, the same layout
as the Hugging Face dataset.

```bash
tasks/latest/<task>/assets/fetch.sh          # = scripts/infrathon/assets.py fetch <task>
scripts/infrathon/assets.py check --all
```

`fetch` downloads our files from `INFRATHON_HF_DATASET` (default
`Infrathon/Infrathon`) or copies them from a local copy
given by `INFRATHON_ASSETS_SOURCE`. Public models and datasets
(`"source": {"kind": "hf", ...}`) come from their own Hugging Face repositories
at a pinned commit, through the normal Hugging Face cache (`HF_HUB_CACHE`,
`HF_HOME`; `assets.py hub-cache` prints it). With the default `"layout":
"cache"` they stay there and tasks mount the cache's repository folder; `"flat"`
also lays them out under the asset root as plain files (hard-linked from the
cache when it is on the same file system). Gated repositories need
`hf auth login` first. `"local-dir"` downloads them straight into the asset root as `hf
download --local-dir` does, keeping the revision records under `.cache/huggingface/`
(Quant-VideoGen checks them). `"kind": "git"` is a public repository checked out at a
pinned commit with its `.git` kept (`"lfs": true` fetches its Git LFS files and needs
`git-lfs`), and `"kind": "url"` one public file from an https URL. These come from their
upstream and are never part of the dataset; the digest of a `local-dir` or `git`
directory leaves out its `.cache/huggingface/` or `.git/` records. An interrupted
download is kept under `<asset root>/.infrathon-partial/` and resumed. Verified directories are stamped under
`<asset root>/.infrathon-verified/` so later checks do not re-hash large models
(`check --full` does); that directory is not part of the dataset. With
`INFRATHON_ASSETS_ROOT` set, a task's `build_images.sh` reads its Judge-only inputs
from the asset root instead of `judge/private/`.

## Large layers

`scripts/infrathon/split_layers.py SOURCE TARGET --workdir DIR [--max-layer-gib 4]`
rewrites an image with the same file system and config, its large layers cut
into parts (the Miles bases are one 50-65 GB layer, fragile to push and pull).
Member headers are kept; a hard link into an earlier part becomes a copy.
Compare `docker export` listings of both images before using the result.

## Host proxy

`scripts/infrathon/host_connect_proxy.py [--port 18080]` is a loopback-only
CONNECT proxy for hosts that reach the internet directly. The concurrent-serving
task needs one on `127.0.0.1:18080` (see its README); it tunnels CONNECT
requests, refuses everything else and keeps idle tunnels open.
